findings.title: maintainability
findings.text: This prefix requires `jobs:` to immediately follow `on: pull_request:`, so it also rejects anything that does not affect the property under test — e.g. a top-level `permissions: { contents: read }` block (the recommended least-privilege placement, currently job-scoped in the workflow) or a `pull_request:` filter (`types:`/`paths:`/`branches:`). A security improvement or an ordinary PR filter would therefore turn this test red even though the trigger is still `pull_request` only. Consider asserting the `on:` block structurally (contains only `pull_request`, unknown triggers rejected) instead of a fixed textual prefix. Not a current failure: the workflow's `permissions:` is job-level, so this passes today.

findings.title: test
findings.text: The section is pinned for many prose claims but not for the exit-code contract that the whole workflow rests on: 0 = report produced, 1 = a `--fail-on` class/flag triggered, 3 = UNVERIFIABLE, 2 = usage error. Since the reason `fetch-depth: 0` matters is precisely that a shallow clone yields exit 3 (UNVERIFIABLE) rather than an empty report, a doc edit that drops that distinction (while keeping the `fetch-depth: 0` phrase) would still pass this test. Add a needle for the exit semantics — e.g. the `UNVERIFIABLE` wording / “cannot be produced” — so the doc keeps the three outcomes distinct.

findings.title: documentation
findings.text: This pair of sentences reads as contradictory for an adopter: `weakened` is put in the `--fail-on` set (so `req diff` exits 1 and, with a required check, blocks the merge), yet the next sentence says it is "not a rejection by req". The docs (`docs/adopting.md`) resolve this with the missing nuance -- loosening is sometimes right, and the point is that it is read on purpose. State that here, or adopters cannot tell whether `weakened` is advisory or blocking in the workflow they just copied.
